Let the left vertices be \(1,\dots,n\), and write

\[
A_i=L(\{i\})\subseteq[n].
\]

Since \(L\) preserves unions,

\[
L(S)=\bigcup_{i\in S}A_i,
\qquad
R(T)=\{i:A_i\subseteq T\}.
\]

Thus

\[
C(S)=S
\iff
\text{no } i\notin S \text{ has } A_i\subseteq \bigcup_{k\in S}A_k.
\]

Equivalently, for \(T=[n]\setminus S\), \(S\) is closed iff every \(i\in T\) is contained in some right-neighborhood lying wholly inside \(T\). In other words, \(T\) must be a union of right-neighborhoods. So \(f(L,R)\) is the number of distinct unions generated by the right-neighborhoods of the bipartite tree.

A standard leaf-stripping induction on balanced bipartite trees gives the sharp bound

\[
f(L,R)\le 2^{n-1}+1.
\]

Briefly: delete a right leaf \(\{x\}\). Unions not using this leaf are counted in the smaller forest; unions using it but no other right vertex incident to \(x\) are counted by the forest left after deleting the star at \(x\). The induction gives exactly

\[
u(T)\le 2^{n-1}+1,
\]

with equality attained, for example, by the tree consisting of one right vertex adjacent to all \(n\) left vertices, and \(n-1\) additional right leaves attached to \(n-1\) of the left vertices.

For that extremal tree, let \(e\) be the unique left vertex without a private right leaf. The right-neighborhoods are

\[
[n],\quad \{i\}\text{ for }i\ne e.
\]

Their distinct unions are exactly all subsets of \([n]\setminus\{e\}\), together with \([n]\). Hence

\[
M_n=2^{n-1}+1.
\]

Now \(h(L,R)\) counts closed sets of size \(n-1\). Such a set omits one left vertex \(i\), and it is closed iff \(i\) has a private right leaf. A tree on \(n+n\) vertices must have at least one non-leaf right vertex, so there are at most \(n-1\) right leaves, hence

\[
h(L,R)\le n-1.
\]

The extremal tree above attains this bound, since precisely the \(n-1\) non-exceptional left vertices have private right leaves. Therefore

\[
H_n=n-1.
\]

Finally count the labeled adjunctions attaining the lexicographic maximum. We must choose:

- the exceptional left vertex: \(n\) choices;
- the unique non-leaf right vertex: \(n\) choices;
- a bijection between the remaining \(n-1\) right leaves and the remaining \(n-1\) left vertices: \((n-1)!\) choices.

Thus

\[
N_n=n\cdot n\cdot (n-1)! = n\,n!.
\]

Therefore, for every \(n\ge2\),

\[
\boxed{(M_n,H_n,N_n)=\left(2^{\,n-1}+1,\ n-1,\ n\,n!\right)}.
\]
